server.name: nyc-record-mcp
server.title: NYC City Record MCP server
server.description: An MCP server for notices published in The City Record, New York City's official newspaper: procurement solicitations and awards, public hearings and meetings, sales and agency rules. Every answer asks the City Record Online dataset on NYC Open Data at the time of the question.

sources.title: City Record notices
sources.what: Notices published in The City Record: solicitations, awards and intents to award or negotiate, public hearings, comment periods and meetings, sales, vendor lists and other notices, each with its agency, dates, title, description, contact and document links, and Changes in Personnel listings.

publisher.name: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services

sources.how_gathered: Read-only requests to the dataset's Socrata API on NYC Open Data (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/dg92-zbpx.json) at the moment you ask, with an app token when SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN is set. Each tool sends one query, such as a keyword search, an agency name, a notice type or a date range, and returns one page of the matching notices exactly as NYC Open Data sends them, in the order the query asks NYC Open Data for: newest publication date (start_date) first, ties broken by the dataset's row id. It asks for one notice more than the limit only to learn whether more are available. BetaNYC's own fields sit beside the notices (showing, offset, more_available, how_to_get_more, a note when a limit was lowered, and source); no notice is dropped, folded, re-sorted or rewritten.

known_gaps: About 88% of the notices in the dataset are 'Changes in Personnel' listings (City staff appointments, departures and pay changes, from July 2013 on). They have no notice type, so get_notices_by_type, get_procurement_notices and get_public_hearings never return them (nor does get_open_solicitations, described under open-solicitations). search_notices, get_notices_by_agency and get_notices_by_date_range do, and personnel listings can fill most of those results.
Personnel listings start in July 2013. Other kinds of notice go back to 2003 at a steady 3,500 to 8,000 a year.

terms.license_name: No restrictions on use: NYC Administrative Code § 23-502(d) (the Open Data Law, Local Law 11 of 2012)
terms.credit_line: Source: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services, City Record Online (NYC Open Data dg92-zbpx).

caveats: Each tool returns at most 100 notices per call (200 for a date range), newest first. When more notices match, the answer says so, and the offset parameter gets the next ones.
An empty answer means no notice in the dataset matched the query, not that no such notice was published. Check City Record Online or the printed City Record before relying on it.
A notice appears only once the agency publishes it in The City Record, which for a public hearing can be about two weeks before the hearing. An agency's own calendar may list a hearing sooner.
City Record Online says questions about the content of a notice go to the agency or contact person named in the notice.

sources.title: Open solicitations, as BetaNYC arranges them
sources.what: Solicitations published in The City Record whose due date has not passed, from the same City Record Online dataset, arranged by BetaNYC: an amended notice folded under the newest notice for the same solicitation, matched cancellations listed apart, and BetaNYC's own labels added to each notice.

publisher.name: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services

sources.how_gathered: Two read-only requests to the dataset's Socrata API on NYC Open Data (https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/dg92-zbpx.json) at the moment you ask, one after the other, with an app token when SOCRATA_APP_TOKEN is set: the solicitations still open, soonest deadline first, and the amended and cancelled solicitations posted in the last 400 days (at most 1,000), which are used only to match notices.

changes.detail: For this list, BetaNYC folds an older notice under a newer one when the PIN (8 characters or more), the agency and the title (without a prefix such as "Bid Extension:") all match, and names the older notice in the newer one's supersedes; moves a matched cancellation, with the notices it cancels, to a separate cancelled list; keeps a notice whose due time is 00:00 (no closing time given) listed through the end of its due date; and adds its own labels under betanyc_notes. Every City field in every row is passed through unchanged, and every row can be seen with include_superseded: true. The official record is the City Record Online dataset: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/dg92-zbpx

known_gaps: Changes in Personnel listings, about 88% of the dataset, have no notice type, so this list never includes them.

Notices count as the same solicitation only when the PIN, agency and title all match, so one solicitation can still appear twice under slightly different titles. Amended and cancelled notices are looked for among those posted in the last 400 days.

terms.license_name: No restrictions on use: NYC Administrative Code § 23-502(d) (the Open Data Law, Local Law 11 of 2012)
terms.credit_line: Source: NYC Department of Citywide Administrative Services, City Record Online (NYC Open Data dg92-zbpx).

caveats: The tool returns at most 100 notices per call, soonest deadline first. offset, limit and more_available count notices as NYC Open Data returns them; the answer says how many were folded or listed as cancelled.

The labels under betanyc_notes (no closing time given, likely placeholder date, extension, correction, cancellation) are BetaNYC's reading of the notice titles and dates, not an official status. Read the notice, or ask the agency, before relying on one.
A due time of 00:00 means the City Record gives no closing time. Check the notice or the agency for the real time.
An empty answer means no notice in the dataset matched the query, not that no such notice was published. Check City Record Online or the printed City Record before relying on it.
City Record Online says questions about the content of a notice go to the agency or contact person named in the notice.
